question.text: Recency bias in investing causes an investor to:

answer.text: Give excessive importance to recent events and trends while underweighting long-term historical data
Fixate on the purchase price of an investment as a reference point
Overestimate their own ability to pick winning investments
Avoid making any investment decisions due to fear of recent market crashes

explanation.text: The Logic: Recency bias makes recent events strongly affect investor decisions — investors extrapolate recent experience and allow it to override analysis, which is why bull markets feel like they will continue and bear markets feel like they will never end. The Trap: Option B describes anchoring bias (fixating on a reference point), Option C describes overconfidence bias, and Option D describes a fear-driven response, not recency bias itself. Note: The defining feature of recency bias is the disproportionate weight placed on recent observations relative to longer-term patterns.
